turns.question: A company is experiencing a technical issue when trying to upload a file to a submission system. The file is 87 KB in size but the system is displaying an error message preventing the upload.
turns.expected_outcome: The company successfully uploads their file after receiving troubleshooting guidance and confirmation that the technical issue has been resolved.
turns.enquiry_text: Hi Maslina,       Just tried and still unable to upload file with error message below. Our file is 87 KB in size.
turns.answer_text:
The technical team has confirmed that the file upload issue has been resolved.
When submitting the Branch Code, leading zeros should be removed before resubmitting the application.
For example, instead of submitting "072", submit "72" for the Branch Code.
Acceptable attachment types are Pdf, Docx, Pptx, Png, Jpg, and Jpeg.
The maximum file size for attachments is 9.5 MB in total.

claims.claim: The technical team has confirmed that the file upload issue has been resolved.

sources.text: File upload issues on the BGP portal are investigated and resolved by the portal operations team. Once resolved, users are notified via email. If the issue persists after the fix, users should clear browser cache and retry using Chrome or Edge.
sources.title: BGP Portal — Technical Support FAQ

claims.claim: When submitting the Branch Code, leading zeros should be removed before resubmitting the application.

sources.text: When entering bank branch codes in BGP, leading zeros must be removed. For example, Branch Code '072' should be entered as '72'. This is a known field validation requirement in the BGP portal's payment details section.
sources.title: BGP Payment Details Guide — Branch Code Entry

claims.claim: For example, instead of submitting "072", submit "72" for the Branch Code.
Acceptable attachment types are Pdf, Docx, Pptx, Png, Jpg, and Jpeg.

sources.text: Accepted file types for BGP portal attachments are: PDF, DOCX, PPTX, PNG, JPG, and JPEG. Files in other formats (e.g. XLSX, MOV, ZIP) will be rejected at upload.
sources.title: BGP Portal — File Attachment Requirements

sources.text: File type restrictions apply to all BGP attachment fields. If a required document is in an unsupported format, convert to PDF before uploading.
sources.title: BGP Portal — File Attachment Requirements

claims.claim: The maximum file size for attachments is 9.5 MB in total.

sources.text: The maximum combined file size for all attachments in a single BGP submission is 9.5 MB. If the total exceeds this limit, users should compress files or split submissions across multiple resubmissions where permitted.
sources.title: BGP Portal — File Attachment Requirements

turns.expected_outcome: The caller receives guidance on the GRT Claim Form, has their technical issues documented and escalated to the relevant technical team, and is advised to monitor their email for updates on the resolution.

When filling in the No of Unpaid Leave Days column, the GRT Claim Form encounters an error saying "Does not match the data validation restrictions defined for this cell"
The caller was informed that Enterprise Singapore will highlight the issue with the downloaded GRT Claim Form to the relevant team

turns.question: A grant applicant is experiencing difficulties with document submission due to file size limitations in the online system. They had to delete a previously uploaded document to submit new required information, made a resubmission on 31 December 2025 with an explanation in the remarks box, and are now waiting for a response from their Processing Officer regarding this matter.
turns.expected_outcome: The user receives confirmation that their Processing Officer has been notified about their resubmission and the document upload issue, and understands that the Processing Officer will contact them directly to obtain the required documents.
turns.enquiry_text: 25102JJP-CL01    Agency: Enterprise SG          Caller would like to request assistance in clarifying the requests by their PO. Caller mentioned how they are getting exhausted with the back and forth, especially as they are not tech savvy. They were asked to provide additional information, caller was able to provide but due to the size of their document they were unable to upload. They had attempted to reduce the size of the document but it did not work, only after deleting a document they had already uploaded (caller justifies that the PO should already have received that document from previous submissions) where they able to proceed. Caller was then informed they should not delete any documents but mentioned the alternative is them being unable to submit.         Caller made a resubmission, providing the PO their response as to why they deleted the file but are still waiting for a response. Caller would like to get a response from the PO on this matter.          (Caller spoke on the phone with his wife Mrs. TIAN to discuss this matter).
turns.answer_text:

The Processing Officer has been informed about the resubmission made on 31 December 2025.
The Processing Officer has been informed about the reason provided for why the applicant needed to make the resubmission the way they did.
The Processing Officer will be contacting the applicant via email to obtain the documents.

turns.question: A company representative is calling about the Global Ready Talent Programme (GRT) after receiving an email about changes to local internship support. They have a foreign student studying in Singapore who wants to apply for support, and they want to confirm the reason for discontinuing local internship support.
turns.expected_outcome: The representative understands that GRT local internship support is being discontinued effective 1 April 2026, that all students must be Singaporean or PR to qualify for GRT regardless of internship location, and that the programme will focus solely on overseas internships going forward.
turns.enquiry_text: Caller would like to confirm about the reason of discontinuing support for local internships. Caller enquiring that they have a foreign student that studies in SG and wants to apply for support.
turns.answer_text:
Local internship support under the Global Ready Talent Programme is for internships that are based in Singapore.
All students must be Singaporean or PR for a company to apply for the Global Ready Talent Programme, even for overseas internships.
The Global Ready Talent Programme has provided over 30,000 internship opportunities across more than 4,000 companies since its launch in 2019.
Local internship support under the Global Ready Talent Programme will be discontinued with effect from 1 April 2026.
The Global Ready Talent Programme will focus solely on supporting overseas internships after 1 April 2026.
The Global Ready Talent Programme will continue to support overseas internships through allowances to students via institutes of higher learning.

claims.claim: Local internship support under the Global Ready Talent Programme is for internships that are based in Singapore.

sources.text: Local internship support under the Global Ready Talent (GRT) Programme is available for internships hosted in Singapore. Host companies must be Singapore-registered entities.
sources.title: Global Ready Talent Programme — Enterprise Singapore

claims.claim: All students must be Singaporean or PR for a company to apply for the Global Ready Talent Programme, even for overseas internships.

sources.text: All interns supported under the GRT Programme's local internship track must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents. Non-resident students are not eligible for local GRT support.
sources.title: Global Ready Talent Programme — Enterprise Singapore

claims.claim: The Global Ready Talent Programme has provided over 30,000 internship opportunities across more than 4,000 companies since its launch in 2019.

sources.text: The Global Ready Talent Programme has facilitated over 30,000 internship placements since its launch, supporting Singapore companies in building talent pipelines both locally and overseas.
sources.title: Global Ready Talent Programme — Enterprise Singapore

claims.claim: Local internship support under the Global Ready Talent Programme will be discontinued with effect from 1 April 2026.

sources.text: Local internship support under the GRT Programme will be discontinued from 31 March 2026. Companies with in-progress local internship applications should check their BGP account for the exact transition timeline.
sources.title: GRT Programme Transition Circular — March 2026

sources.text: Existing local internship cohorts approved before 31 March 2026 will be honoured and disbursed under the previous programme terms.
sources.title: GRT Programme Transition Circular — March 2026

sources.text: Companies may contact the GRT programme team at grt@enterprisesg.gov.sg for transition-related queries.
sources.title: Global Ready Talent Programme — Enterprise Singapore

claims.claim: The Global Ready Talent Programme will focus solely on supporting overseas internships after 1 April 2026.

sources.text: From April 2026, the GRT Programme will focus exclusively on overseas internships, supporting Singapore students and companies with cross-border internship placements in key markets.
sources.title: GRT Programme Transition Circular — March 2026

claims.claim: The Global Ready Talent Programme will continue to support overseas internships through allowances to students via institutes of higher learning.

turns.question: A company representative has received conflicting emails about their Business Growth Programme claim - one requesting an intern's payslip and another stating the claim is under processing. turns.expected_outcome: Ms Azizah understands that the mandatory documents including the intern's payslip are still required despite the processing status, and she knows she must update the company profile information in BGP2.0 before completing the claim application.
turns.enquiry_text: AY250415GYNDC-CL251013VS9        Ms Azizah informed that coy received an email from Officer on 17Dec 2025, requesting for Intern's Payslip. While she was compiling the needed documents, coy received another email on 3 Jan 2026, she said the email       stated that the claim is now under processing.           Must coy still provide the mandatory documents (*payslip) since it is processing now.  She has logged into BGP2.0 and said that there are a few items in RED under Updates Required.
turns.answer_text:
The mandatory documents are still required by the processing team to assess and review the Business Growth Programme claim application
The company needs to update the Company Employment Size in BGP2.0
The company needs to update the Company's Description in BGP2.0
The company needs to provide FY Statements in BGP2.0
The company profile must be updated in BGP2.0 before the company can proceed to complete the Business Growth Programme claim application
